title: The Goalkeeper (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 98bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal football patience solitude
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The goalkeeper is the only player allowed to use their hands
And for ninety minutes
Mostly they don't need to
Mostly they stand and watch eleven other people
Have all the feelings

[Verse 2]
The goalkeeper is a specialist in waiting
In the particular alertness of someone
Who might be needed urgently at any moment
Or not at all
But must act as if both are equally likely

[Chorus]
The goalkeeper says — I am ready
The goalkeeper says — I have been ready since the whistle
The goalkeeper says — the ball will come here eventually
And when it does
I will have the only opinion that matters

[Bridge]
Chas said — the goalkeeper's job is concentration without event
Most people can concentrate when things are happening
The goalkeeper concentrates through the absence of things happening
That is the harder skill
And nobody talks about it at half time

[Verse 3]
When the goalkeeper makes the save the crowd erupts
When the goalkeeper doesn't touch the ball for eighty-nine minutes
Nobody mentions it
The goalkeeper understands this
The goalkeeper chose this

[Outro]
The goalkeeper
The goalkeeper
That's my boy
